title: Two Sum
prompt: Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to `target`. Each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice. Return the two indices in any order.

title: Valid Parentheses
prompt: Given a string `s` containing only the characters `()[]{}`, return `true` if every bracket is closed by the same type of bracket in the correct order, and `false` otherwise. An empty string is valid.

title: Binary Search
prompt: Given a sorted array of distinct integers `nums` and a `target`, return the index of `target`, or `-1` if it is not present. Aim for O(log n) time.

title: Climbing Stairs
prompt: You are climbing a staircase with `n` steps. Each time you can climb 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you reach the top?

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
prompt: Given a string `s`, return the length of the longest substring that contains no repeated characters.

title: Merge Intervals
prompt: Given a list of intervals `[start, end]`, merge all overlapping intervals (touching intervals such as `[1,4]` and `[4,5]` overlap) and return the merged intervals sorted by start.

title: Group Anagrams
prompt: Given a list of strings, group the anagrams together. Return the groups in any order; the words inside a group may also be in any order.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
prompt: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k` most frequent elements, in any order. The answer is guaranteed to be unique.

title: Product of Array Except Self
prompt: Given an integer array `nums`, return an array where element `i` is the product of all elements except `nums[i]`, without using division, in O(n) time.

title: Maximum Subarray
prompt: Given a non-empty integer array `nums`, find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum and return that sum.

title: Second Highest Salary
prompt: Table `employees(id, name, salary)`. Return one row with one column, `second_highest`: the second highest **distinct** salary, or `NULL` if there isn't one.

tests.schema:
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, salary INTEGER);
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Ana',100),(2,'Ben',200),(3,'Cy',300),(4,'Di',300);

CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, salary INTEGER);
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Ana',100),(2,'Ben',100);

title: Customers Who Never Ordered
prompt: Tables `customers(id, name)` and `orders(id, customer_id)`. Return the `name` of every customer who has never placed an order, in any order.

title: Top Earner per Department
prompt: Tables `departments(id, name)` and `employees(id, name, salary, department_id)`. For each department, return `department`, `employee` and `salary` for its highest-paid employee(s); include ties. Any row order.

title: Running Total of Sales
prompt: Table `sales(day, amount)` with one row per day (`day` is an ISO date). Return `day` and `running_total` (sum of `amount` up to and including that day), ordered by `day`.

tests.schema:
CREATE TABLE sales (day TEXT PRIMARY KEY, amount INTEGER);
INSERT INTO sales VALUES ('2026-01-03',30),('2026-01-01',10),('2026-01-02',20);

CREATE TABLE sales (day TEXT PRIMARY KEY, amount INTEGER);
INSERT INTO sales VALUES ('2026-02-01',5);
